_about: Changes that alter how agents behave. A new install starts with each one on. An install that already has agents gets each new entry switched off and waiting for its owner's decision: its lead agent reviews the change for that install and explains it, and the owner turns it on or leaves it off on the /changes page, or asks the lead in their own message to do it (behaviour_change, only for entries with leadMay true). leadMay is false for anything about security or spending limits: only the owner switches those, on the page. Add an entry here for any future change to agent behaviour; never switch one on for existing installs by itself.

changes.title: Team advice in agents' instructions
changes.changes: Adds a short "running a team" section to agents' instructions: when to do a job themselves and when to hand it to a worker, which kind of model suits which job, how to write a brief, and how to get a second opinion and a critical check from a different model. Lead agents get the full version, other agents a core version, small local models and members' agents a short one. Turning it on gives it to the lead and to agents created from then on; agents that already exist get it only when it is switched on for them one by one (agent settings, Team guidance).
changes.benefits: Agents that hand out work do it more often and better: cheaper models for routine work, the strongest model kept for planning and hard reviews, important work checked by a second model before it is relied on.
changes.costs: About 450 words more in each lead turn's instructions (about 120 for the short version), and some extra worker or reviewer runs where an agent decides a job needs them.
changes.check: Which agents here already hand out work (consult_agent, spawn_workers) and how; whether their own instructions already cover delegation; which agents would benefit most (usually the primary agents that do long or many-part jobs).
changes.on: The lead and new agents get it; existing agents when switched on one by one.

changes.title: A starter team: a Challenger and three workers
changes.changes: Offers to create four agents: a Challenger that reviews important work adversarially, Scout for lookups and summaries, Builder for coding and multi-step work, Researcher for research and writing. They use cheaper models on the plans this install already pays for; the Challenger uses another company's model where one is connected. Turning it on shows a Set up your team card; nothing is created until the owner presses Create there. An agent name that is already taken is skipped.
changes.benefits: The lead has ready workers to hand routine work to and a second model to check important work, without setting them up by hand.
changes.costs: Each agent uses its model when it is given work; one billed per use is marked on the card before anything is created.
changes.check: Whether agents with these roles already exist here (a reviewer, a quick helper, a coder, a researcher), which models the workers would get, and whether any would be billed per use.
changes.on: The Set up your team card appears for an admin; agents are created only from it.
changes.off: No card and no starter agents.

changes.title: A spending limit: members' temporary helpers use only the models members may choose
changes.changes: This is a spending limit on family members' agents, not a change to your own agents. A member's agent can start temporary helpers for parts of a job. With this on, those helpers may run only on that agent's own model and the models the admin lets members choose for their own agents (the members' model list); any other model is refused. (The member limits on reasoning and speed apply to their helpers either way.) With it off, a member's temporary helpers may use any model this install reaches, as before.
changes.benefits: Members can't spend the owner's money on models the admin didn't allow them, for example a top model billed per use.
changes.costs: A member's agent that relied on a model outside the list for its workers gets a refusal naming the allowed models; the admin may need to add a model to the members' list.
changes.check: Whether this install has members, which models their agents use, what the members' model list holds, and whether members' agents start temporary helpers today. It limits spending; it does not change how the owner's own agents work.
changes.on: Members' temporary helpers are limited to the agent's own model and the members' model list.
changes.off: Members' temporary helpers may use any model this install reaches.

changes.title: The lead suggests new workers from how the install is used
changes.changes: Once a week the lead looks at a summary of how agents were used in the past seven days (requests per agent and model, errors, temporary workers it keeps starting) and, when a pattern would be better served by a permanent worker or specialist, proposes one to the owner in plain words: its name, job, model and what it would save or improve. At most one short proposal at a time; it builds one only on the owner's yes. For members' agents it uses counts only, never their conversations.
changes.benefits: Repeated work moves to the right agent and model over time instead of the lead redoing it, or a top model spending itself on routine jobs.
changes.costs: One short lead turn a week; occasionally a proposal to read.
changes.check: How busy this install is, whether the owner wants suggestions, and which agents do repeated work on expensive models.
changes.on: A weekly look and at most one proposal at a time (how often: weekly or off, set on this page).
changes.off: No weekly look and no proposals.

changes.title: Primary agents ask the lead for workers they need
changes.changes: Adds one line to primary agents' instructions: when they need a worker or a specialist they don't have, they ask the lead (by name) with the job, a proposed name and the model tier they think it needs; the lead decides with the owner. A member's main agent asks through its existing request to an admin instead, and a member's other agents ask that member's main agent; they never reach the admin's agents.
changes.benefits: Gaps in the team surface to the lead and the owner instead of an agent struggling on its own.
changes.costs: Now and then a request for the lead to answer.
changes.check: Which primary agents exist here and whether the lead should hear from them.

changes.title: Primary agents keep long work on track with check-ins
changes.changes: When a primary agent starts or hands off work that will outlast its reply (a project another agent leads, a background job, a batch of workers, anything expected to take more than about 15 minutes), it schedules its own check-in: every 30 minutes by default, sooner for short jobs, less often for overnight work, and only one per piece of work. Each check-in reads the status cheaply, unblocks or answers what is waiting, tells you only about a decision you must make, a blocker or the finished work, and cancels itself when the work is done. Work that shows no progress across two check-ins is reported to you in plain words. The lead gets the full instructions, other primary agents a short version.
changes.benefits: Long work doesn't quietly stall: someone looks at it on a schedule, unblocks it, and you hear about it when it matters, not all the time.
changes.costs: A short turn of the agent's model at each check-in while work is running (with the default, two an hour per piece of work), and about 150 words more in the lead's instructions (about 70 for other primary agents). Members' main agents get it too, on the models you allow them.
changes.check: Whether agents here start long work (projects led by other agents, background jobs, batches of workers), whether they already schedule their own follow-ups, and whether the owner wants fewer or more updates.
changes.on: Primary agents schedule and run check-ins on their long work.
changes.off: Agents follow up only when they decide to on their own.

changes.title: Primary agents suggest better ways of working
changes.changes: When a primary agent sees a better way to get your kind of work done, it says so in one or two lines and asks: a specialist for a subject that keeps coming back, a dedicated lead agent for a long project so your main agent stays free, a batch of low-cost helpers for work that can run in parallel, a cheaper model or speed for routine jobs, a scheduled task instead of a manual repeat, a Record for facts it keeps asking for again, or anything else that would make things easier for you. At most one suggestion per topic and only when it is relevant; after a no it remembers and does not suggest it again; nothing is created without your yes, and new agents are built by the lead (a member's agent asks through its request to an admin).
changes.benefits: Your agents get better at your work over time and point out savings you might not know about, without you having to know what is possible.
changes.costs: About 170 words more in each primary agent's instructions; now and then a one- or two-line suggestion to answer (at most one per conversation); a yes may add an agent or a scheduled task. Members' main agents get it too; theirs ask an admin through their request.
changes.check: How the owner uses the primary agents today, whether there are repeated jobs or long projects that a specialist, a project lead or cheaper models would serve better, and whether the owner welcomes suggestions.
changes.on: Primary agents make short suggestions when they are relevant.
changes.off: No suggestions about better ways of working.
